verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents built-in OAuth/OIDC handling: social sign-on providers, an SSO plugin supporting OIDC and OAuth2 providers, an MCP plugin that acts as an OAuth authorization server, and the RFC 8628 device grant. A community member also reports it acting as an OIDC provider. However, nothing in the pack explicitly covers authorization code with PKCE or OAuth refresh-token handling; the documented session refresh is a session feature, not OAuth refresh tokens. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of authorization-code-with-PKCE support, OAuth refresh token issuance/rotation, independent hands-on corroboration of those flows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can implement standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows (authorization code with PKCE, refresh tokens) without hand-rolling protocol details

citations.quote: This plugin supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), OAuth2 providers, and SAML 2.0.
Better Auth supports multiple social providers, including Google, GitHub, Apple, Discord, and more.
The **MCP** plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) clients.
The Device Authorization plugin implements the code issuance and approval flow from the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant
acting as an identity provider and OIDC/SSO provider
